neighbours.label: the word that completes a reciprocal relation between two things ('related to each other', 'bound up together', 'connected')
fire: The two theories turned out to be closely related to each other.
In her view, memory and identity are woven together from the start.
Rainfall and crop yield were strongly correlated with one another.
The old villages gradually merged together into a single town.
Both problems are linked by a common cause in the supply chain.
The characters' fates are deeply intertwined with each other.
Over the years, the two companies became tightly connected.
These muscles and tendons are bound together by thin fibers.
quiet: The two theories turned out to be developed in different decades.
In her view, memory fades slowly from the start.
Rainfall was measured every morning at the station.
The old villages gradually lost most of their residents.
Both problems were reported last week in the supply chain.
The other characters appear only in the final chapter.
Over the years, the two companies grew much larger.
We went to the market together on Saturday morning.

notes: Card: ' other' x7 (each other), ' together' x4, ' by', ' another', ' connected', after relate/correlate/merge/bind. Near misses keep the topics but state no mutual relation, or use 'other'/'together' without reciprocity.
